issues.t: Timing chain stretch on the 3.0L V6
issues.sym: Check engine light with codes such as P0008 or P0017, a rattle at startup, rough running, reduced engine power, or stalling. Owners report it between about 55,000 and 120,000 miles.
issues.why: The timing chains stretch over time, so the camshafts fall out of step with the crankshaft. Long oil change intervals make it worse.
issues.next: Don't ignore P0008/P0016/P0017 codes. Get a diagnosis soon, because a chain that jumps can damage the engine. Change oil on time with the correct dexos oil.

issues.t: Timing chain problems on the 3.6L V6
issues.sym: Check engine light, sluggish running, misfires or a rattle from the engine.
issues.why: Owners of first-generation SRXs with the 3.6L V6 report stretched timing chains and worn tensioners, sometimes at fairly low mileage.
issues.next: Have the codes read and the timing checked if the light comes on with cam/crank correlation codes. Keep up with oil changes.

issues.t: Automatic transmission failure
issues.sym: The transmission slips, won't shift, or quits suddenly, sometimes with no warning while stopped.
issues.why: Owners of early SRXs report transmission failures, often between about 50,000 and 100,000 miles.
issues.next: Check the fluid and get a transmission diagnosis at the first sign of slipping or harsh shifts. A rebuild or replacement is usually needed once it fails.

issues.t: Water or condensation inside the headlights
issues.sym: Fog or water inside the headlight lens, dim or dead low beams, and a bulb-out warning, often worse after rain or in cold weather.
issues.why: The headlight housings let moisture in. The water dims the light and can short out the bulbs and electronics.
issues.next: Don't wait, since poor headlights are a safety risk. A new headlight assembly is the usual fix. Ask a Cadillac dealer whether a goodwill repair applies; some owners report GM helped with the repair.

issues.t: Low-beam headlights too dim
issues.sym: The low beams light up very little of the road, even with new bulbs.
issues.why: Owners report the headlight projectors or lenses dim with age, and many complaints come from second-generation SRXs.
issues.next: Try new quality bulbs first and check the lenses for haze or moisture. If that doesn't help, the headlight assembly usually has to be replaced.

issues.t: CUE touchscreen stops responding or cracks
issues.sym: The CUE infotainment screen ignores touches, presses things on its own, or develops a spiderweb crack.
issues.why: The touch layer on the CUE screen separates and fails with heat and age.
issues.next: A shop can replace just the touch panel instead of the whole radio.

issues.t: Service Rear Axle warning on AWD models
issues.sym: A 'Service Rear Axle' message on the dash, sometimes with AWD not working.
issues.why: Owners report faults in the rear drive unit that controls the all-wheel-drive system.
issues.next: Have the codes read. Ask the dealer about fluid service or software updates for the rear drive module before replacing parts.

issues.t: Ratcheting noise from the transfer case
issues.sym: A ratcheting or clicking noise from under the car, especially when turning or pulling away.
issues.why: Owners of early AWD SRXs report noise from the transfer case and differential.
issues.next: Have the transfer case and differential fluid checked and the noise diagnosed before the part fails.

issues.t: Brakes and rotors wear out early
issues.sym: Grinding, pulsing in the brake pedal, or pads and rotors needing replacement much sooner than expected.
issues.why: Owners report short life from the original pads and rotors on this heavy SUV.
issues.next: Have the brakes checked at every oil change. Quality pads and rotors usually last longer than the originals.

issues.t: Wheel hub bearing failure
issues.sym: A humming or growling noise that rises with speed, sometimes with an ABS light.
issues.why: The wheel hub bearings wear out, often around 70,000-80,000 miles.
issues.next: Have the noisy corner identified and the hub replaced. Don't wait until it gets loud, since a failed bearing affects handling.

issues.t: A/C compressor failure
issues.sym: The A/C blows warm, or you hear noise when the A/C kicks on.
issues.why: Owners report the A/C compressor failing at fairly low mileage.
issues.next: Have the system checked for a leak and the compressor tested. When a compressor fails, the system should be flushed before the new one goes in.

issues.t: Catalytic converter failure
issues.sym: Check engine light, a rotten-egg smell, rattling under the car, or weak acceleration.
issues.why: Owners report catalytic converters failing around 50,000 miles. Misfires or oil burning can also ruin a converter.
issues.next: Have the codes read and fix any misfire first. Then replace the failed converter.

issues.t: Tires wearing out early
issues.sym: Tires wear unevenly or need replacing well before their rated life.
issues.why: Owners report early tire wear, which usually points to alignment settings or worn suspension parts on a heavy vehicle.
issues.next: Get an alignment check and rotate the tires regularly.

issues.t: Engine burning oil
issues.sym: The oil level drops between changes, sometimes with blue smoke or a low-oil warning.
issues.why: Owners report excessive oil consumption on 2008 SRXs at fairly low mileage.
issues.next: Check the oil every fill-up and keep it topped up. Ask the dealer to run an oil consumption test.

issues.t: Engine revs and lurches forward while stopped
issues.sym: The engine suddenly revs and the SUV pushes forward while you are stopped with your foot on the brake.
issues.why: Owners report sudden high idle or surging on 2008 SRXs. Throttle body or idle control faults are common suspects.
issues.next: Hold the brake firmly and shift to neutral if it happens. Have the throttle body and engine computer checked right away.

issues.t: Unintended acceleration complaints
issues.sym: The SUV speeds up on its own or keeps accelerating when you lift off the gas.
issues.why: Owners of 2009 SRXs report unintended acceleration. Floor mats, a sticking pedal or throttle body faults are common causes to rule out.
issues.next: Remove any extra floor mats, then have the pedal and throttle body checked. Report it to NHTSA if it happens.

issues.t: Sunroof leaks water inside
issues.sym: Water drips from the headliner, wet carpets or a musty smell after rain.
issues.why: The large sunroof's drain tubes clog or come loose, so water overflows into the cabin.
issues.next: Have the sunroof drains cleared and checked. Dry the carpet quickly to stop mold and electrical problems.

issues.t: Brake assist warning
issues.sym: A service brake assist warning on the dash, sometimes with a harder brake pedal.
issues.why: Owners report brake assist faults on high-mileage 2009 SRXs.
issues.next: Have the brake system scanned for codes. Get it fixed soon if the pedal feels different.

issues.t: Rear differential pinion seal leak
issues.sym: Oil drips or wetness at the rear differential, sometimes with a whine or hum.
issues.why: Owners report rear pinion seal leaks, and GM recalled many SRXs for rear drive axle seal leaks.
issues.next: Check for open recalls first. Have the seal replaced and the differential refilled before it runs low on oil.

issues.t: Ignition switch can turn off while driving (recall)
issues.sym: The engine can shut off while driving if the key is bumped or heavy items hang from it, and airbags may not work.
issues.why: The ignition switch can slip out of the run position, cutting power and turning off the airbags.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 14V394 and have the free repair done. Until then, keep only the ignition key on the ring.

issues.t: Rear differential seal leak can cause loss of power (recall)
issues.sym: Oil leaking from the rear axle area, noise from the rear, or a sudden loss of drive power.
issues.why: A leaking rear drive axle seal lets differential oil escape until the differential fails.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 07V589. The dealer repair is free.

issues.t: Shift lever may not hold in Park (recall)
issues.sym: The SUV may roll after being shifted to Park, especially on a slope.
issues.why: A problem with the transmission shift lever can let the vehicle roll when parked.
issues.next: Always use the parking brake and check your VIN for recall 08V527.

issues.t: Front lower control arm nut can come loose (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking from the front end, or in the worst case the wheel tilts and drags.
issues.why: The ball joint nut and washer on the front lower control arm could loosen, letting the arm separate from the knuckle.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 04V273 and have the free repair done.

issues.t: ABS problem can lengthen stopping distance (recall)
issues.sym: Braking feels weaker than expected or stops take longer.
issues.why: A fault in the anti-lock brake system could increase stopping distance.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 04V151.

issues.t: Harder brake pedal from throttle control software (recall)
issues.sym: The brake pedal needs more force and stops take longer.
issues.why: The electronic throttle control could keep the engine from returning fully to idle during braking.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 05V046.

issues.t: Front seat can pivot back in a crash (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom before a crash.
issues.why: The front bucket seat attachments may not hold the seat in some crashes.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 03V346.

issues.t: Rear toe link can loosen and separate (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking from the rear, wandering at highway speed, or poor steering response.
issues.why: A rear suspension toe link can loosen and come apart, which can cause loss of control.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 21V473 and have the free repair done right away.

issues.t: Rear toe adjuster link may be loose (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking from the rear or the SUV wandering.
issues.why: The rear toe adjuster link may not have been tightened properly.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 14V571.

issues.t: Turbo V6 engine damage on low-octane fuel (recall)
issues.sym: A knocking or pinging noise under load.
issues.why: On the 2.8L turbo V6, using less than premium fuel could cause detonation that breaks a piston or connecting rod.
issues.next: Use premium fuel and check your VIN for recall 10V223. Stop driving if loud knocking starts.

issues.t: Power steering line can leak and cause fire (recall)
issues.sym: A burning smell, smoke from under the hood, or fluid under the car.
issues.why: A power steering pressure line can leak fluid onto hot engine parts.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 10V450.

issues.t: Shifter can show Park when it isn't (recall)
issues.sym: The shifter won't move out of gear, or shows Park when the transmission isn't in Park.
issues.why: A shift cable or control fault could let the SUV roll away.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 11V595 and always set the parking brake.

issues.t: Driver seat can drop suddenly (recall)
issues.sym: The driver's seat suddenly drops down.
issues.why: A seat height adjuster bolt can fall out.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 14V447.

issues.t: Acceleration delay from transmission software (recall)
issues.sym: A delay of several seconds before the SUV accelerates.
issues.why: Transmission software could cause a lag in response.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 14V212; the dealer updates the software.

issues.t: Lug nuts may loosen (recall)
issues.sym: Clicking or wobbling from a wheel.
issues.why: Lug nuts could loosen, break studs and let a wheel come off.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 13V202.

issues.t: Loss of engine braking (recall)
issues.sym: The SUV coasts more than expected when you lift off the gas.
issues.why: A transmission problem could cause unexpected loss of engine braking.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 13V097.
